A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text and appendices A–I. Figure 4's graphic is absent from v3 despite its caption and discussion; its inclusion in v4 is a directly observable document difference.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments measuring how cognitive-bias attacks affect LLM product recommendations, including controlled datasets, Amazon products, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and their numerical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The expert sentence-appending attacks, Claude-generated description rewrites, recommendation procedure, and defensive prompting are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic coffee machines, cameras, and books, plus Amazon laptops and chew toys. The English-language recommendation tasks and test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated expert/generated attacks, unattacked controls, and LLaMA, Claude, and Mistral models are unchanged. The supplied Figure 4 does not establish an expanded comparator set.

E3.justification: The ten-product pools, shuffled inputs, model configurations, recommendation metrics, and price, rating, reasoning, and defense evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 supplies quantitative evidence for the existing Section 4.1 analysis of products becoming the most frequently recommended after attacks. Its question and qualitative findings were already present; the other ablations and robustness analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same repetition counts, attack-variant information, statistical-significance reporting, and standard deviations. Figure 4 introduces no additional uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v4 makes Figure 4's model-by-bias counts available, including 6 products for LLaMA-405b and 1 for Mistral under expert social proof. v3 contains only the caption and qualitative discussion. Existing tables and other plotted results are unchanged; this is additional reporting, not an established performance improvement.

T1.justification: The metric and attack-success definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain identical claims about cognitive-bias attacks, model susceptibility, and mitigation difficulties.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model differences, reasoning and defense failures, and weaker effects on Amazon data are unchanged. The limitations concerning broad queries, English descriptions, small product pools, and preliminary defenses are also retained.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, prompts, description-generation instructions, output parsing, dataset details, and code-access information are unchanged, including the appendix disclosures.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior recommendation attacks are identical. The bibliography only reflows across pages.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes. All substantive wording, headings, terminology, and section order are retained; there is no substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 has a Figure 4 caption without its chart on page 6; v4 includes the grouped bar chart with that caption on page 7. This causes subsequent page reflow. Other graphics, table designs, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Supplying the missing Figure 4 fixes an incomplete presentation and lets readers inspect the numerical evidence behind the existing top-recommendation analysis. This is a useful but limited improvement; the methods, remaining evidence, claims, and appendices are unchanged.
